actions.content:
build a minimal web app called “fabnetwork.app”

goal:
a map-based interface to discover fabrication-capable locations (makerspaces, libraries, labs) in a single city (san francisco for v0)

core concept:
inspired by queeringthemap.com — a full-screen map with clickable pins

scope (v0):

* no accounts
* no login
* no payments
* no job submission
* no backend database required
* static or API-fetched data only

features:

1. map interface

* full screen interactive map (mapbox or leaflet)
* centered on san francisco
* no location permissions required
* user can pan/zoom freely

2. pins (main feature)

* each pin represents a place with fabrication capability:

  * makerspaces
  * libraries
  * school labs (optional)

* different icons:

  * library icon
  * makerspace icon

3. pin interaction

* clicking a pin opens a small tooltip / popup card

* tooltip includes:

  * name of place
  * type (library / makerspace)
  * capabilities:

    * 3d printing
    * resin printing
    * cnc
    * pcb
    * laser cutting
    * cricut / vinyl cutting
  * membership info:

    * free / public
    * monthly fee (if known)

* keep tooltip minimal and readable

4. data source

* start with a small hardcoded dataset OR fetch from:

  * public libraries api (if available)
  * manually curated makerspace list

* structure:

  * name
  * lat/lng
  * type
  * capabilities (array)
  * membership_cost (string)

5. design

* minimal UI
* map-first, no clutter
* no sidebar required
* soft, clean markers
* inspired by queeringthemap interaction model

6. philosophy

* discovery only
* no data collection
* no user tracking
* no forms
* no persistence

future (do not build yet):

* routing jobs to creators
* local creator network (local.fabnetwork.app)
* payments
* lockers and delivery

tech:

* frontend only (react or vite js)
* use mapbox or leaflet
* no heavy backend

goal:
a working prototype where users can explore fabrication locations in san francisco and click pins to see capabilities and access info
8. backend (minimal, no auth)

this app uses a lightweight backend for data, but has no user accounts or authentication.

data:

* store a list of fabrication locations (makerspaces, libraries)
* each location includes:

  * name
  * coordinates (lat/lng)
  * type (library / makerspace)
  * capabilities (array: cnc, 3d printer, resin, etc.)
  * membership info
  * source link

api:

* GET /locations → returns all locations
* no user-specific data

submissions:

* allow users to suggest edits via a simple form

form fields:

* location name
* suggested change (text)
* source URL (required)
* optional notes

behavior:

* submissions are NOT auto-applied
* they are stored for review
* no login required to submit

constraints:

* no authentication system
* no user profiles
* no tracking of who submitted what beyond optional text input
* treat this like a public “tip line” rather than a wiki account system

input.name: fabnetwork.app — SF Fabrication Map
input.content:
## Summary

A full-screen, map-based discovery tool for fabrication-capable locations in San Francisco — makerspaces, public libraries with equipment, and labs. Users can explore pins on the map, click them to see capabilities and access info, and submit tips about new or changed locations. No accounts, no login, no tracking.

---

## How it will work

### Map view
- The app opens to a full-screen interactive map centered on San Francisco
- Users can pan and zoom freely — no location permission requested
- Pins are placed on the map for each known fabrication location
- Two pin styles: one for **libraries**, one for **makerspaces** (distinct icons/colors)

### Pin interaction
- Clicking a pin opens a small popup card anchored to the pin
- The card shows:
  - **Name** of the location
  - **Type** (Library / Makerspace)
  - **Capabilities** displayed as tags: 3D Printing, Resin Printing, CNC, PCB, Laser Cutting, Cricut/Vinyl Cutting
  - **Membership info**: e.g. "Free / Public" or "$50/month"
  - An optional **source link** for more info
- Clicking elsewhere on the map closes the popup

### Suggest a change (tip line)
- A small, unobtrusive button in a corner of the map opens a modal form
- Users can submit:
  - Location name (required)
  - Suggested change (text, required)
  - Source URL (required)
  - Optional notes
- Submissions are stored for admin review — not auto-applied
- No login required; no submitter identity is tracked

---

## Data details

A **Locations** database table will store all fabrication sites:
- Name, latitude, longitude
- Type (library / makerspace)
- Capabilities (multi-select)
- Membership cost (text, e.g. "Free" or "$75/mo")
- Source link (URL)

A **Submissions** table will store user-suggested edits:
- Location name, suggested change, source URL, optional notes
- Submitted at (timestamp)

The app will ship with a small curated seed dataset (~10–15 SF locations) pre-loaded into the database.

A backend endpoint serves all locations (`GET /locations`) so data can be updated without redeploying the frontend.

---

## Assumptions

- **Leaflet** will be used for the map (open-source, no API key required). If you prefer Mapbox, an API key will be needed.
- The initial dataset is manually curated — no live sync with external APIs (library APIs, etc.) in v0.
- Submissions are stored but there's no admin UI to review them yet (that's a future feature).
- The map tiles use OpenStreetMap (free, no key needed).

---

## Not included (v0)

- Admin review interface for submissions
- Auto-population from public library APIs
- User accounts, login, or any form of identity
- Payments, job routing, or delivery features

2. **Pins**: Large black teardrop/location pins (not circles)
3. **Top left**: Hamburger menu icon (☰) in a square border
4. **Top center**: "QUEERING THE MAP" in bold serif/display font
5. **Top right**: Plus/add icon (+) in a square border
6. **Bottom right**: Controls - location button (circle with dot), zoom in (+), zoom out (-), and info (ⓘ) button

For fabnetwork.app, I'm adapting this same layout but replacing the plain black pins with teardrop shapes containing lucide icons (makerspace and library icons). For the pins, I need teardrop-shaped markers with icons inside them. Since I can't render React components directly in Leaflet's divIcon, I'll embed SVG paths for lucide icons as HTML strings instead. I'm thinking of using book-open for libraries and wrench for makerspaces.
